| a worrying rise | une hausse inquiétante |
| once rare | autrefois rare |
| a neighbourhood | un quartier |
| a burden | un fardeau |
| yet | pourtant |
| to tax | taxer |

### Stratégie de lecture

1. **Skimming** (lecture globale) : titre + premières phrases → idée générale.
2. **Scanning** (lecture ciblée) : chercher une information précise (un nom, un chiffre, un exemple).
3. **Deviner un mot inconnu** grâce au contexte avant d'ouvrir le dictionnaire : dans « a worrying rise in obesity », rise est suivi d'une maladie qui augmente… donc rise = hausse.

### Questions

Les questions (compréhension globale, détaillée, vocabulaire en contexte et interprétation) sont dans les **exercices 5 et 6**, en bas de page.

lessons.title: Speaking — Giving opinions and debating with respect
lessons.content:
## Speaking — S'exprimer à l'oral

### 1. Discussion questions — Questions de discussion

Réponds à voix haute en phrases complètes, en donnant ton opinion.

1. Is voting important? Why do some people not vote?
2. What must a good class delegate do? What mustn't he or she do?
3. Should voting be compulsory?
4. How can young people take part in public life without being politicians?
5. How can we fight fake news on social media?

### 2. Phrases modèles — Exprimer et nuancer son opinion

| Pour… | Phrases |
|---|---|
| Donner son avis | In my opinion,… / I think that… / I believe that… / As far as I'm concerned,… |
| Être d'accord | I agree with you. / That's a good point. / Exactly! |
| Ne pas être d'accord poliment | I'm not sure I agree. / I see your point, but… / I'm afraid I disagree. |
| Nuancer | It depends on… / To some extent,… / On the one hand,… on the other hand,… |
| Exprimer une obligation | Citizens must… / Leaders have to… / We mustn't… |

### 3. Rules of the class — La charte de la classe (1 minute 30)

En groupe, rédigez la **charte de vie de la classe** : cinq règles avec **must** ou **have to**, trois interdictions avec **mustn't**, deux choses facultatives avec **don't have to**. Un porte-parole la présente à la classe.

Exemple : « We must arrive on time. We mustn't use our phones during lessons. We don't have to wear a tie on Fridays. »

### 4. Role-play — L'élection des délégués

**Student A et Student B — candidates.** Chacun prépare un discours de 1 minute avec trois promesses précises et réalistes, en utilisant must, have to, will.

**The class — voters.** Posez une question à chaque candidat, puis votez à bulletin secret.

### 5. Débat

**Motion :** « Young people should take part in politics. »

- **For :** les décisions les concernent (école, emploi), les jeunes sont nombreux, ils apportent des idées nouvelles, la démocratie a besoin de tous.
- **Against :** priorité aux études, manque d'expérience, risque de manipulation, il y a d'autres façons de s'engager (associations, bénévolat).

### Règles du débat respectueux

- On critique **les idées**, jamais **les personnes**.
- On attend son tour : you mustn't interrupt.
- On justifie chaque opinion par un argument et un exemple.
- Ce débat est un exercice d'expression : aucune opinion partisane n'est attendue ni notée.

lessons.title: Speaking — Talking about your eating habits
lessons.content:
## Speaking — S'exprimer à l'oral

### 1. Discussion questions — Questions de discussion

Réponds à voix haute, en faisant des phrases complètes. Utilise au moins un modal par réponse.

1. What do you usually eat for breakfast, lunch and dinner?
2. Do you think young people in Congo eat better or worse than their grandparents? Why?
3. What advice would you give to a friend who drinks too many sodas?
4. Should street food be sold near schools? Give two reasons.
5. What do you do to stay fit?

### 2. Phrases modèles — Model sentences

Répète ces phrases jusqu'à les dire sans lire :

| Pour… | Phrases |
|---|---|
| Parler de ses habitudes | I usually have… for breakfast. / I never skip lunch. / I eat fish twice a week. |
| Donner un conseil | You should… / You ought to… / If I were you, I would… / You'd better… |
| Donner son avis | In my opinion,… / I think that… / I strongly believe that… |
| Être d'accord ou non | I agree with you because… / I'm not sure about that. / I disagree, because… |
| Nuancer | It depends on… / On the one hand,… on the other hand,… |

### 3. Role-play — Jeu de rôle

Travaillez à deux. Inversez ensuite les rôles.

**Student A — the patient.** You often feel tired, you have headaches and you have gained weight. You eat fried food every day and you never exercise. Explain your problem and ask for advice.

**Student B — the doctor.** Ask questions about the patient's habits (sleep, food, drinks, sport). Then give at least **four pieces of advice** using should, ought to, had better and must.

Pour commencer :
- **Doctor:** Good afternoon. What can I do for you?
- **Patient:** Good afternoon, doctor. I've been feeling tired and…

### 4. Mini-débat

**Motion :** « Sugary drinks should be banned in schools. »

Formez deux groupes (for / against). Chaque groupe prépare trois arguments avec un exemple, puis répond aux arguments de l'autre groupe. Utilisez les connecteurs first, moreover, however, finally.

### Conseils pour l'oral

- Parle lentement et articule les fins de mots (diet, healthy, vitamins).
- Accentue la bonne syllabe : ˈhealthy, preˈvent, ˈvegetables (3 syllabes : /ˈvedʒtəblz/).
- Mieux vaut une phrase simple et juste qu'une phrase longue et fausse.

lessons.title: Vocabulary — Development, growth and poverty
lessons.content:
## Vocabulary — Le vocabulaire de l'unité

Apprends ces mots par groupes de 10. Lis chaque exemple à voix haute.

### 1. The economy — L'économie

| English | Prononciation | Français | Catégorie | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| development | /dɪˈveləpmənt/ | le développement | nom | Development is not only about money. |
| a developing country | /dɪˈveləpɪŋ/ | un pays en développement | nom | Congo is a developing country. |
| a developed country | /dɪˈveləpt/ | un pays développé | nom | Germany is a developed country. |
| growth | /ɡrəʊθ/ | la croissance | nom | Economic growth has been slow this year. |
| wealth | /welθ/ | la richesse | nom | Oil has brought wealth to some people. |
| poverty | /ˈpɒvəti/ | la pauvreté | nom | Many families still live in poverty. |
| income | /ˈɪnkʌm/ | le revenu | nom | The average income is low in rural areas. |
| resources | /rɪˈsɔːsɪz/ | les ressources | nom | Congo is rich in natural resources. |
| investment | /ɪnˈvestmənt/ | l'investissement | nom | Foreign investment creates jobs. |
| debt | /det/ | la dette | nom | Debt is a heavy burden for poor countries. |
| aid | /eɪd/ | l'aide (internationale) | nom | Aid helped to build the new hospital. |
| unemployment | /ˌʌnɪmˈplɔɪmənt/ | le chômage | nom | Unemployment is high among young people. |

### 2. Human development — Le développement humain

| English | Prononciation | Français | Catégorie | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| the standard of living | /ˈstændəd əv ˈlɪvɪŋ/ | le niveau de vie | nom | The standard of living has risen in towns. |
| life expectancy | /laɪf ɪkˈspektənsi/ | l'espérance de vie | nom | Life expectancy has increased since 2000. |
| literacy / illiteracy | /ˈlɪtərəsi/ | l'alphabétisation / l'analphabétisme | nom | Literacy is the ability to read and write. |
| the literacy rate | /ˈlɪtərəsi reɪt/ | le taux d'alphabétisation | nom | The literacy rate is high in Congo. |
| education | /ˌedʒuˈkeɪʃn/ | l'éducation, l'enseignement | nom | Education is a human right. |
| health care | /ˈhelθ keə/ | les soins de santé | nom | Health care is expensive in the cities. |
| clean / drinking water | /kliːn ˈwɔːtə/ | l'eau potable | nom | Many villages still lack drinking water. |
| infrastructure | /ˈɪnfrəstrʌktʃə/ | les infrastructures | nom | Roads and bridges are infrastructure. |
| electricity | /ɪˌlekˈtrɪsəti/ | l'électricité | nom | Electricity has reached the village. |
| the HDI (Human Development Index) | /ˌeɪtʃ diː ˈaɪ/ | l'IDH (indice de développement humain) | nom | The HDI combines income, health and education. |

### 3. Verbs and expressions — Verbes et expressions

| English | Prononciation | Français | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| to develop | /dɪˈveləp/ | (se) développer | Countries develop thanks to education. |
| to improve | /ɪmˈpruːv/ | améliorer, s'améliorer | Living conditions have improved. |
| to increase / to decrease | /ɪnˈkriːs/ /dɪˈkriːs/ | augmenter / diminuer | Poverty has decreased in the capital. |
| to reduce | /rɪˈdjuːs/ | réduire | We must reduce inequalities. |
| to build (built, built) | /bɪld/ | construire | They have built a new bridge. |
| to provide | /prəˈvaɪd/ | fournir | The project provides clean water. |
| to fight against | /faɪt əˈɡenst/ | lutter contre | We must fight against corruption. |
| to rely on | /rɪˈlaɪ ɒn/ | dépendre de, compter sur | Congo relies on oil exports. |
| to be in debt | /bi ɪn det/ | être endetté | Many countries are in debt. |
| sustainable development | /səˈsteɪnəbl/ | le développement durable | Sustainable development protects the future. |
| good governance | /ɡʊd ˈɡʌvənəns/ | la bonne gouvernance | Good governance attracts investors. |
| the gap between rich and poor | /ɡæp/ | l'écart entre riches et pauvres | The gap between rich and poor is growing. |

### 4. Word families — Les familles de mots

Repérer la famille d'un mot aide à deviner le sens d'un mot inconnu :

| Verbe | Nom | Adjectif |
|---|---|---|
| to develop | development | developed / developing |
| to grow | growth | growing |
| to improve | improvement | improved |
| to invest | investment / investor | — |
| to educate | education | educated / educational |
| — | poverty | poor |
| — | wealth | wealthy |

**Attention aux faux amis :** « actually » = en fait (et non « actuellement », qui se dit currently ou nowadays) ; « eventually » = finalement (et non « éventuellement »).

### Mémorisation

Classe les mots dans ton carnet en deux colonnes : **progrès** (growth, improve, investment…) et **problèmes** (poverty, debt, unemployment…). Revois-les le lendemain, puis après 3 et 7 jours.

lessons.title: Grammar — Talking about results: the present perfect
lessons.content:
## Grammar — Faire un bilan : le present perfect

Quand on parle du développement, on fait souvent le **bilan** de ce qui a changé jusqu'à aujourd'hui : « le pays a construit des routes », « la vie s'est améliorée depuis 2010 ». En anglais, on utilise le **present perfect**.

### 1. Observe — Observe d'abord

Phrases tirées du reportage de l'unité :

- The village **has changed** a lot in five years.
- We **have built** a new school.
- I **have lived** here **since** 1998.
- The children **haven't had** any cases of cholera **for** two years.
- **Have** you **received** help from the government? — Not **yet**.

Toutes ces phrases relient le **passé** au **présent** : l'action a eu lieu avant, mais son résultat compte maintenant.

### 2. La formation

**have / has + participe passé**

| Forme | Construction | Exemple |
|---|---|---|
| Affirmative | sujet + have / has + participe passé | The government **has built** a dam. |
| Négative | sujet + haven't / hasn't + participe passé | Poverty **hasn't disappeared**. |
| Interrogative | Have / Has + sujet + participe passé ? | **Has** life **improved**? |

- I / you / we / they → **have** ('ve) ; he / she / it → **has** ('s).
- Verbes réguliers : participe passé en **-ed** (improve → improved, increase → increased).
- Verbes irréguliers à connaître : build → **built**, grow → **grown**, become → **become**, bring → **brought**, make → **made**, give → **given**, go → **gone**, have → **had**, see → **seen**, spend → **spent**.

### 3. Les emplois

| Emploi | Mots-clés | Exemple |
|---|---|---|
| **Bilan, résultat présent** d'une action passée | — | The country has built many schools. (les écoles existent aujourd'hui) |
| **Action qui dure encore** | **since** + point de départ ; **for** + durée | I have lived in Pointe-Noire since 2015 / for ten years. |
| **Expérience** (déjà / jamais) | ever, never | Have you ever visited a dam? — I have never seen one. |
| **Action récente ou attendue** | already, just, yet | The water has just arrived. They haven't finished the road yet. |

### 4. Since ou for ?

- **since** + **point de départ** (une date, un moment) : since 2010, since independence, since last year, since I was a child.
- **for** + **durée** : for ten years, for three months, for a long time.
- En français on dit « depuis » dans les deux cas : « J'habite ici depuis 2015 / depuis dix ans » → I have lived here **since 2015** / **for ten years**. Attention : jamais le présent simple (I live here since 2015 est faux).

### 5. Present perfect ou prétérit ?

| Present perfect | Prétérit (simple past) |
|---|---|
| Moment **non précisé** ou période **pas terminée** | Moment **précis** et **terminé** |
| The government **has built** a new hospital. | The government **built** a new hospital **in 2019**. |
| Life **has improved** this year. (l'année n'est pas finie) | Life **improved** last year. |

Avec **yesterday, last year, in 2010, ago, when…**, on emploie le **prétérit**, jamais le present perfect.

### 6. Cinq exemples sur le thème

1. Congo **has become** an oil-producing country.
2. Literacy **has increased** since the 1960s.
3. Many young people **have left** the villages for the cities.
4. The new road **has reduced** the journey time.
5. **Have** the rural areas **benefited** from growth? — Not enough.

### 7. Erreurs fréquentes

| Faux | Correct | Pourquoi |
|---|---|---|
| I live here since 2015. | I have lived here since 2015. | action qui dure → present perfect |
| They have built the school in 2019. | They built the school in 2019. | date précise → prétérit |
| She has went to Brazzaville. | She has gone to Brazzaville. | participe passé de go = gone |
| He have improved his results. | He has improved his results. | he → has |
| I have lived here since ten years. | I have lived here for ten years. | durée → for |
| Did you ever see a dam? | Have you ever seen a dam? | expérience → present perfect |

### À toi

Les exercices de grammaire corrigés sont dans le bouton « Exercices » en bas de page (exercices 1 à 3).

lessons.title: Listening — A well, a school and a solar panel
lessons.content:
## Listening — Un reportage radio

**Situation :** Une journaliste de radio, Nadia, interroge Monsieur Ngoma, chef d'un village du département des Plateaux, sur les changements apportés par un projet de développement.

### Avant d'écouter

1. Mots-clés : a well (un puits), a solar panel (un panneau solaire), cholera (le choléra), a cooperative (une coopérative), a dirt road (une piste en terre).
2. Devine : qu'est-ce qu'un puits, une école et un panneau solaire peuvent changer dans un village ?

### Comment travailler

L'enregistrement audio sera bientôt disponible dans l'application. En attendant :

- **Première écoute :** fais-toi lire le dialogue par un camarade, sans le regarder, et réponds aux questions globales (exercice 4, partie A).
- **Deuxième écoute :** relis le texte et réponds aux questions de détail.
- **Troisième écoute :** lis-le à deux en jouant les rôles.

### Transcript — Transcription

**Nadia:** Good morning, Mr Ngoma. Thank you for welcoming us. How long have you been the chief of this village?

**Mr Ngoma:** Good morning. I have been the chief for twelve years, and I have lived here since I was born.

**Nadia:** People say that the village has changed a lot. What has changed?

**Mr Ngoma:** Oh, many things! Five years ago, the women walked four kilometres every day to get water from the river. Then an association built a well in the centre of the village. Since then, nobody has walked to the river for water.

**Nadia:** What difference has it made?

**Mr Ngoma:** A huge difference. The children haven't had any cases of cholera for two years. And the girls, who used to carry water all morning, now go to school.

**Nadia:** Speaking of school, I can see a new building over there.

**Mr Ngoma:** Yes. The parents and the government have built a primary school with three classrooms. Before, the children studied under a mango tree. This year, forty pupils have passed the CEPE — it's a record for our village!

**Nadia:** Congratulations. And that solar panel on the roof?

**Mr Ngoma:** That's our latest project. We have installed two solar panels for the health centre and the school. The nurse can now keep vaccines cold, and the pupils can study in the evening.

**Nadia:** Has everything improved, then?

**Mr Ngoma:** Not everything. The road is still a dirt road, and in the rainy season trucks can't come. So our farmers can't sell their cassava in Brazzaville. We have asked for a new road many times, but nothing has happened yet.

**Nadia:** What are your plans for the future?

**Mr Ngoma:** We have just created a farmers' cooperative. Together, the farmers can buy a small truck and get better prices. Development doesn't fall from the sky: we have learnt that we must work together.

**Nadia:** Thank you very much, Mr Ngoma.

### Vocabulaire clé du reportage

| English | Français |
|---|---|
| How long have you been… ? | Depuis combien de temps êtes-vous… ? |
| to welcome | accueillir |
| used to carry | portaient autrefois |
| a classroom | une salle de classe |
| a record | un record |
| to keep vaccines cold | garder les vaccins au froid |
| the rainy season | la saison des pluies |
| a farmer | un agriculteur |
| to get better prices | obtenir de meilleurs prix |
| to fall from the sky | tomber du ciel |

**Remarque :** repère dans le dialogue les phrases au present perfect (have been, has changed, have built…) et celles au prétérit avec un repère passé (Five years ago, the women walked…). C'est exactement la différence étudiée en grammaire.

### Questions

Les questions de compréhension et leur corrigé sont dans l'**exercice 4**, en bas de page.

lessons.title: Reading — What does development really mean?
lessons.content:
## Reading — Comprendre un texte

### Avant de lire — Skimming

Lis le titre et la première phrase de chaque paragraphe. Selon toi, quelle est l'idée principale du texte ?

### What does development really mean?

**1.** For a long time, development was measured only by money. Economists compared the Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of countries: the richer a country was, the more "developed" it was said to be. But money alone does not tell us whether people can read, see a doctor or drink clean water. A country can produce a lot of oil and still have many poor citizens.

**2.** In 1990, the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) created a new tool: the Human Development Index (HDI). It combines three things: income, life expectancy and education. Since then, the HDI has changed the way the world looks at development. It has shown that some countries with modest incomes have achieved good results in health and education, while some rich countries have left many people behind.

**3.** Africa illustrates this paradox. The continent is rich in oil, minerals, forests and fertile land, yet it remains the poorest region of the world. In many countries, the wealth from natural resources has not reached ordinary people. Roads, schools and hospitals are still lacking in rural areas, and young people often cannot find jobs.

**4.** Nevertheless, much progress has been made. Since the 1960s, literacy rates have increased considerably, and many more children, especially girls, have gone to school. Mobile phones have transformed daily life, and in several countries poverty has decreased. The challenge now is to turn natural resources into lasting benefits: good schools, health care, infrastructure and jobs.

**5.** This is what "sustainable development" means: meeting the needs of today's generation without destroying the resources that future generations will need. Cutting down the forests or polluting the rivers may bring money today, but it will make tomorrow poorer. True development, therefore, is not just about becoming richer. It is about allowing every person to live a longer, healthier and freer life.

(Texte rédigé pour ce cours, environ 350 mots.)

### Mots utiles du texte

| English | Français |
|---|---|
| Gross Domestic Product (GDP) | le produit intérieur brut (PIB) |
| a tool | un outil |
| to combine | associer, combiner |
| to achieve | atteindre, réaliser |
| to leave behind | laisser de côté |
| fertile land | des terres fertiles |
| yet / nevertheless | pourtant / néanmoins |
| lacking | manquant |
| lasting benefits | des bénéfices durables |
| to meet the needs | répondre aux besoins |

### Stratégie de lecture

1. **Skimming** : titre + premières phrases → idée générale.
2. **Scanning** : cherche une information précise (une date, un sigle, un chiffre). Ex. : en quelle année l'IDH a-t-il été créé ?
3. **Les connecteurs** guident la lecture : yet et nevertheless annoncent une opposition, therefore une conclusion.

### Questions

Les questions de compréhension, de vocabulaire et d'interprétation sont dans les **exercices 5 et 6**, en bas de page.

lessons.title: Grammar — Telling the past: simple past and used to
lessons.content:
## Grammar — Raconter le passé : prétérit et used to

Pour raconter la carrière d'un artiste ou un souvenir de match, on a besoin de deux outils : le **prétérit** pour les **événements terminés** et **used to** pour les **habitudes passées** (qui n'existent plus).

### 1. Observe — Observe d'abord

Phrases tirées de l'interview de l'unité :

- I **started** athletics when I was eleven.
- Last year I **won** the gold medal in the 100 metres.
- I **didn't have** proper shoes at the beginning.
- I **used to run** barefoot on the beach.
- My mother **didn't use to** like sport, but now she comes to every race.

### 2. Le prétérit (simple past) — Événements terminés

| Forme | Construction | Exemple |
|---|---|---|
| Affirmative | verbe + **-ed** (réguliers) ou 2e forme (irréguliers) | She **trained** hard. They **won** the cup. |
| Négative | **didn't** + base verbale | They **didn't win**. (et non didn't won) |
| Interrogative | **Did** + sujet + base verbale ? | **Did** you **watch** the match? |

**Verbes irréguliers indispensables pour ce thème :**

| Base | Prétérit | Français |
|---|---|---|
| win | won | gagner |
| lose | lost | perdre |
| beat | beat | battre |
| become | became | devenir |
| begin | began | commencer |
| sing | sang | chanter |
| write | wrote | écrire |
| run | ran | courir |
| take | took | prendre |
| go | went | aller |
| break | broke | briser, battre (un record) |
| feel | felt | ressentir |

**Mots-clés du prétérit :** yesterday, last week / year, in 1972, two years ago, when I was a child.

### 3. Used to — Habitudes et états passés

**used to + base verbale** exprime ce qui se faisait **régulièrement** dans le passé et **ne se fait plus** (ou une situation passée qui a changé).

| Forme | Construction | Exemple |
|---|---|---|
| Affirmative | used to + base verbale | I **used to play** football every evening. |
| Négative | didn't use to + base verbale | She **didn't use to** like rap. |
| Interrogative | Did + sujet + use to + base verbale ? | **Did** you **use to** sing in a choir? |

Le français utilise souvent l'**imparfait** : « je jouais au football tous les soirs » → I used to play football every evening.

### 4. Prétérit ou used to ?

| Prétérit | Used to |
|---|---|
| Un événement unique ou daté | Une habitude répétée, terminée |
| Congo **won** the African Cup of Nations in 1972. | Children **used to** make footballs with old clothes. |
| I **went** to a rumba concert last Saturday. | I **used to** go to concerts every week before the exam year. |

Le prétérit peut aussi exprimer une habitude (I played football every day), mais **used to** insiste sur le contraste avec aujourd'hui.

### 5. Cinq exemples sur le thème

1. The Diables Rouges **won** the African Cup of Nations in 1972.
2. Rumba musicians **used to** play in the bars of Poto-Poto and Bacongo.
3. She **didn't give up** after her injury.
4. **Did** you **use to** dance at school parties?
5. He **broke** the national record two years ago.

### 6. Erreurs fréquentes

| Faux | Correct | Pourquoi |
|---|---|---|
| They didn't won the match. | They didn't win the match. | après didn't → base verbale |
| Did she sang well? | Did she sing well? | après did → base verbale |
| I use to play football when I was young. | I used to play football when I was young. | habitude passée → used to |
| He is used to play the guitar. | He used to play the guitar. | be used to + -ing = être habitué à (autre sens) |
| I used to playing football. | I used to play football. | used to + base verbale |
| Congo used to win the cup in 1972. | Congo won the cup in 1972. | événement unique et daté → prétérit |

### Pour aller plus loin : be used to + -ing

Attention : **be used to + -ing** signifie « être habitué à » : I'm used to training early in the morning (je suis habitué à m'entraîner tôt). C'est une autre structure, à ne pas confondre avec used to + base verbale.

### À toi

Les exercices de grammaire corrigés sont dans le bouton « Exercices » en bas de page (exercices 1 à 3).

lessons.title: Listening — Running for a dream
lessons.content:
## Listening — Une interview

**Situation :** Dans une émission sportive, le journaliste Patrick interroge Mireille, 19 ans, sprinteuse de Pointe-Noire, championne nationale du 100 mètres.

### Avant d'écouter

1. Mots-clés : a sprinter (une sprinteuse), barefoot (pieds nus), a scholarship (une bourse), an injury (une blessure), to qualify (se qualifier).
2. Devine : quelles difficultés une jeune athlète congolaise peut-elle rencontrer ?

### Comment travailler

L'enregistrement audio sera bientôt disponible dans l'application. En attendant :

- **Première écoute :** fais-toi lire l'interview sans la regarder ; réponds aux questions globales (exercice 4, partie A).
- **Deuxième écoute :** relis le texte, puis réponds aux questions de détail.
- **Troisième écoute :** lis-la à deux en jouant les rôles.

### Transcript — Transcription

**Patrick:** Mireille, congratulations! You are the national champion of the 100 metres. How did it all begin?

**Mireille:** Thank you! I started athletics when I was eleven. At that time, I used to run on the beach in Pointe-Noire every evening with my brothers. We used to race against each other, and I usually won!

**Patrick:** Did you have a coach at the beginning?

**Mireille:** No, I didn't. A PE teacher noticed me at a school competition and took me to a club. I didn't have proper running shoes, so I used to run barefoot. My first coach gave me my first pair of spikes.

**Patrick:** Was your family happy about your choice?

**Mireille:** Not really. My mother didn't use to like sport. She wanted me to study and become a nurse. She used to say, "Sport doesn't feed people." But now she comes to every race and she shouts louder than everybody!

**Patrick:** What was the most difficult moment of your career?

**Mireille:** Two years ago, I had a bad injury to my knee. I couldn't run for six months. I felt very sad and I almost gave up. But my coach told me, "Champions are not the ones who never fall, they are the ones who get up." So I trained again, slowly, and last year I won the gold medal at the national championship.

**Patrick:** And what about school?

**Mireille:** I passed my baccalaureate last June. It wasn't easy: I used to revise in the bus on the way to training. Now I have a scholarship to study and train abroad.

**Patrick:** What is your dream?

**Mireille:** To qualify for the African Games and, one day, the Olympic Games. And I want to show the girls of my neighbourhood that sport and school can go together.

**Patrick:** Thank you, Mireille, and good luck!

### Vocabulaire clé de l'interview

| English | Français |
|---|---|
| to race against each other | faire la course les uns contre les autres |
| a PE teacher (Physical Education) | un professeur d'EPS |
| to notice | remarquer |
| spikes / running shoes | des pointes / des chaussures de course |
| to shout | crier |
| an injury to the knee | une blessure au genou |
| to get up | se relever |
| a scholarship | une bourse d'études |
| abroad | à l'étranger |
| to go together | aller de pair |

**Remarque :** repère les prétérits (started, gave, had, won, passed) et les « used to » (used to run, used to race, used to revise) : Mireille distingue ses habitudes d'autrefois des événements marquants de sa carrière.

### Questions

Les questions de compréhension et leur corrigé sont dans l'**exercice 4**, en bas de page.

lessons.title: Reading — Congolese rumba, a heritage of humanity
lessons.content:
## Reading — Comprendre un texte

### Avant de lire — Skimming

Lis le titre et la première phrase de chaque paragraphe. Quel est le sujet du texte ?

### Congolese rumba, a heritage of humanity

**1.** In December 2021, UNESCO inscribed Congolese rumba on its list of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity. The nomination was presented jointly by the Republic of the Congo and the Democratic Republic of the Congo, the two countries that face each other across the Congo River. For the people of Brazzaville and Kinshasa, it was a moment of great pride: their music was now recognised as a treasure of the whole world.

**2.** Congolese rumba was born in the 1940s and 1950s in the two capitals. Local musicians used to listen to Cuban records that arrived on ships, and they mixed these Latin rhythms with traditional Congolese songs and dances. Bars and dance halls in Poto-Poto, Bacongo or Kinshasa became the cradle of a new music. Famous orchestras appeared, such as Les Bantous de la Capitale, founded in Brazzaville in 1959, and OK Jazz in Kinshasa.

**3.** At first, rumba was simply music for dancing and celebrating. But it soon became much more. Singers used to compose songs about love, but also about social life, politics and independence. In the 1960s, rumba accompanied the birth of the new nations, and its guitars spread across the continent. Later, it gave birth to faster styles like soukous and ndombolo, which young people still dance today.

**4.** Today, rumba is part of family events, weddings and funerals. It is taught in music schools and played by young artists who mix it with hip-hop or afro-pop. However, some musicians worry that the new generation listens only to foreign music and forgets the old masters. They believe that the UNESCO recognition must be followed by real action: archives, museums, and support for young musicians.

**5.** Like football, rumba shows that culture can unite people across borders. When a rumba song plays, nobody asks whether the dancers come from Brazzaville or Kinshasa. As one old guitarist said, "Rumba was born on both banks of the river, and it belongs to everybody."

(Texte rédigé pour ce cours, environ 340 mots.)

### Mots utiles du texte

| English | Français |
|---|---|
| to inscribe | inscrire |
| intangible heritage | le patrimoine immatériel |
| jointly | conjointement |
| across the river | de part et d'autre du fleuve |
| a record (here) | un disque |
| the cradle | le berceau |
| to found (founded) | fonder |
| to spread (spread) | se répandre |
| to give birth to | donner naissance à |
| a bank (of a river) | une rive |

### Stratégie de lecture

1. **Skimming** : repère le sujet et l'organisation (histoire, évolution, situation actuelle).
2. **Scanning** : relève les dates (2021, 1940s, 1959, 1960s) et ce qui s'est passé à chacune.
3. **Attention au double sens** : « record » signifie ici un disque, pas un record sportif. Le contexte (« Cuban records that arrived on ships ») lève l'ambiguïté.

### Questions

Les questions sont dans les **exercices 5 et 6**, en bas de page.

lessons.title: Speaking — Sharing memories and opinions
lessons.content:
## Speaking — S'exprimer à l'oral

### 1. Discussion questions — Questions de discussion

Réponds à voix haute en phrases complètes. Emploie le prétérit ou used to quand tu parles du passé.

1. What games did you use to play when you were a child?
2. Tell us about a match or a concert you remember. What happened?
3. Who is your role model in music or sport? Why?
4. Can sport or music be a real job in Congo? Why or why not?
5. Should schools give more time to sport and music?

### 2. Phrases modèles — Model sentences

| Pour… | Phrases |
|---|---|
| Raconter un souvenir | I remember the day when… / It happened in… / First,… then,… in the end,… |
| Parler d'une habitude passée | When I was younger, I used to… / We used to… every Sunday. |
| Exprimer ses goûts | I'm keen on… / I'm really into… / I can't stand… |
| Donner son avis | As far as I'm concerned,… / I'm convinced that… |
| Débattre | That may be true, but… / I see what you mean, however… |

### 3. Raconte un souvenir — Storytelling (1 minute 30)

Raconte **un moment fort** lié à la musique ou au sport : un match gagné ou perdu, un concert, une fête de quartier. Utilise au moins **cinq verbes au prétérit** et **une phrase avec used to**. Ton camarade te pose ensuite deux questions (Did you…? Why did you…?).

### 4. Role-play — Interview d'une star

**Student A — journalist.** Prépare six questions sur la carrière d'un artiste ou d'un sportif congolais (réel ou imaginaire) : débuts, difficultés, plus grande victoire, projets.

**Student B — the star.** Réponds en racontant ton parcours au prétérit et avec used to.

### 5. Débat

**Motion :** « Young people should be encouraged to become professional musicians or athletes. »

- **For :** passion, talent, fierté nationale, possibilité de carrière internationale, modèles pour la jeunesse.
- **Against :** peu de réussites, carrières courtes, risques de blessure, importance des études et d'un métier sûr.

### Conseils pour l'oral

- Prononce les prétérits en -ed : played /d/, practised /t/, started /ɪd/.
- Ne prononce pas « used to » comme « use-ed » : on dit /ˈjuːstə/.
- Raconte avec des connecteurs de temps : at first, then, after that, finally, in the end.

lessons.title: Reading — Citizens, not spectators
lessons.content:
## Reading — Comprendre un texte

### Avant de lire — Skimming

Lis le titre et la première phrase de chaque paragraphe. Qui sont les trois jeunes présentés ? Que font-ils pour leur communauté ?

### Citizens, not spectators

**1.** Many young people say that politics is "not for them". They see it as a game for adults, made of long speeches and broken promises. Yet politics, in its original meaning, is simply the organisation of life in the city: who decides, how decisions are made, and how the common good is protected. Every decision, from the price of bread to the number of teachers in a school, is a political decision. As a famous saying goes, "If you don't do politics, politics will be done without you."

**2.** The word "democracy" comes from Greek and means "power of the people". In a democracy, citizens elect their representatives through free and fair elections, and those representatives have to be accountable: they must explain their decisions and respect the constitution. But democracy is not only about voting once every few years. Citizens have rights, such as freedom of speech and equality before the law, and they also have duties: they must obey the law, pay their taxes and respect the opinions of others.

**3.** Some young Africans have decided to act. Armel, 20, voted for the first time last year. "I had to queue for two hours in the sun," he says, "but I was proud. My grandparents didn't always have this chance." Nadège, 22, is a member of her neighbourhood committee in Pointe-Noire. With other volunteers, she meets the local council every month to discuss rubbish collection and street lighting. "You don't have to be a minister to change things," she says.

**4.** Others fight a new enemy: false information. Every day, rumours and fake news spread on social media, especially before elections. Christ, 24, a young journalist, runs a page that checks viral messages. "Before sharing a message, you must ask three questions: who wrote it, where does it come from, and is it confirmed by a serious source? A citizen mustn't be a megaphone for lies."

**5.** Democracy is never finished; it has to be built every day, by leaders who serve and by citizens who take part. Being a citizen does not mean agreeing with everybody: it means debating with respect, refusing violence and corruption, and keeping the common good in mind. Young people are not the leaders of tomorrow only. They are already the citizens of today.

(Texte rédigé pour ce cours, environ 390 mots.)

### Mots utiles du texte

| English | Français |
|---|---|
| a spectator | un spectateur |
| a broken promise | une promesse non tenue |
| the original meaning | le sens premier |
| a representative | un représentant |
| free and fair elections | des élections libres et transparentes |
| to obey | obéir à |
| to queue | faire la queue |
| a neighbourhood committee | un comité de quartier |
| street lighting | l'éclairage public |
| fake news / a rumour | les fausses nouvelles / une rumeur |
| viral | viral |
| a megaphone | un mégaphone, un porte-voix |

### Stratégie de lecture

1. **Skimming** : le texte suit le plan définition de la politique → démocratie, droits et devoirs → exemples de jeunes engagés → désinformation → conclusion.
2. **Scanning** : pour chaque jeune (Armel, Nadège, Christ), relève l'âge et la forme d'engagement.
3. **Repère les modaux** : have to be accountable, must explain, must obey, had to queue, don't have to be, must ask, mustn't be, has to be built.

### Questions

Les questions sont dans les **exercices 5 et 6**, en bas de page.

lessons.title: Vocabulary — Food, diet and health
lessons.content:
## Vocabulary — Le vocabulaire de l'unité

Apprends ces mots par petits groupes de 10. Lis chaque exemple à voix haute. La prononciation est notée entre barres obliques (alphabet phonétique) ; la syllabe accentuée est précédée de ˈ.

### 1. Food and nutrients — Aliments et nutriments

| English | Prononciation | Français | Catégorie | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| a balanced diet | /ə ˈbælənst ˈdaɪət/ | une alimentation équilibrée | nom | A balanced diet gives you energy all day. |
| a meal | /miːl/ | un repas | nom | We have three meals a day. |
| nutrients | /ˈnjuːtriənts/ | les nutriments | nom | Vegetables are full of nutrients. |
| vitamins | /ˈvɪtəmɪnz/ | les vitamines | nom | Oranges contain a lot of vitamins. |
| proteins | /ˈprəʊtiːnz/ | les protéines | nom | Beans and fish are rich in proteins. |
| fat | /fæt/ | les graisses, le gras | nom | Fried food contains too much fat. |
| sugar | /ˈʃʊɡə/ | le sucre | nom | Sodas contain a lot of sugar. |
| salt | /sɔːlt/ | le sel | nom | Too much salt is bad for the heart. |
| junk food | /ˈdʒʌŋk fuːd/ | la malbouffe | nom | Junk food is cheap but unhealthy. |
| fresh | /freʃ/ | frais | adjectif | Buy fresh fish at the market. |
| greens / leafy vegetables | /ɡriːnz/ | les légumes verts (saka-saka, ngaï-ngaï…) | nom | Cassava leaves are healthy greens. |
| a staple food | /ˈsteɪpl fuːd/ | un aliment de base | nom | Cassava is a staple food in Congo. |

### 2. Health and illness — Santé et maladie

| English | Prononciation | Français | Catégorie | Example |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| healthy / unhealthy | /ˈhelθi/ | sain, en bonne santé / malsain | adjectif | Walking is a healthy habit. |
| a disease / an illness | /dɪˈziːz/ /ˈɪlnəs/ | une maladie | nom | Malaria is a dangerous disease. |
| overweight | /ˌəʊvəˈweɪt/ | en surpoids | adjectif | He became overweight after years of junk food. |
| obesity | /əʊˈbiːsəti/ | l'obésité | nom | Obesity is growing in African cities. |
| malnutrition | /ˌmælnjuːˈtrɪʃn/ | la malnutrition | nom | Malnutrition affects many young children. |
| diabetes | /ˌdaɪəˈbiːtiːz/ | le diabète | nom | Too much sugar can lead to diabetes. |
| high blood pressure | /haɪ blʌd ˈpreʃə/ | l'hypertension | nom | Salt can cause high blood pressure. |
| a symptom | /ˈsɪmptəm/ | un symptôme | nom | Fever is a symptom of malaria. |
| a treatment | /ˈtriːtmənt/ | un traitement | nom | The doctor prescribed a treatment. |
| hygiene | /ˈhaɪdʒiːn/ | l'hygiène | nom | Good hygiene prevents many diseases. |

### 3. Useful verbs and expressions — Verbes et expressions

| English | Prononciation | Français | Example |
|---|---|---|---|
| to eat well | /iːt wel/ | bien manger | Students need to eat well to study well. |
| to skip a meal | /skɪp ə miːl/ | sauter un repas | Don't skip breakfast before school. |
| to gain / to lose weight | /ɡeɪn/ /luːz weɪt/ | prendre / perdre du poids | She lost weight by walking every day. |
| to prevent | /prɪˈvent/ | prévenir, empêcher | Vaccines prevent diseases. |
| to recover | /rɪˈkʌvə/ | guérir, se rétablir | He recovered quickly after treatment. |
| to exercise | /ˈeksəsaɪz/ | faire de l'exercice | You should exercise three times a week. |
| to stay fit | /steɪ fɪt/ | rester en forme | Football helps me stay fit. |
| to be on a diet | /bi ɒn ə ˈdaɪət/ | être au régime | My uncle is on a diet: no more sugar. |
| to see a doctor | /siː ə ˈdɒktə/ | consulter un médecin | If the fever continues, see a doctor. |
| to prescribe | /prɪˈskraɪb/ | prescrire | The doctor prescribed some tablets. |
| Prevention is better than cure. | — | Mieux vaut prévenir que guérir. | — |
| You are what you eat. | — | On est ce que l'on mange. | — |

### 4. Countable or uncountable? — Dénombrable ou non ?

En anglais, beaucoup d'aliments sont **indénombrables** : on ne peut pas les compter, donc pas de « s » au pluriel ni de « a/an ».

| Dénombrables (a / many / a few) | Indénombrables (some / much / a little) |
|---|---|
| an orange, two bananas, many eggs, a few tomatoes | rice, bread, water, sugar, salt, meat, fish (aliment), fruit, food |
| How **many** eggs? | How **much** water? |

**À retenir :** on dit some bread ou a piece of bread, some rice ou a plate of rice, jamais « a bread » ni « rices ».

### Mémorisation

Recopie chaque jour 10 mots dans ton carnet de vocabulaire, avec leur exemple. Revois-les le lendemain, puis 3 jours et 7 jours plus tard : c'est la **répétition espacée**, la méthode la plus efficace pour retenir.

lessons.title: Grammar — Giving advice: should, ought to, had better, must
lessons.content:
## Grammar — Donner un conseil

Quand on parle de santé, on donne sans cesse des conseils : « tu devrais manger plus de fruits », « tu ferais mieux de voir un médecin ». En anglais, on utilise pour cela des **modaux**.

### 1. Observe — Observe d'abord

Lis ces phrases tirées du dialogue de l'unité :

- **You should** eat more fruit and vegetables.
- **You ought to** drink more water.
- **You'd better** see a doctor if the fever comes back.
- **You must** take this medicine twice a day.
- **You shouldn't** skip breakfast.

Quel mot suit chaque modal ? Toujours un **verbe à la base verbale**, sans « to » (sauf ought to) et sans « s ».

### 2. La règle

| Modal | Sens | Force | Exemple |
|---|---|---|---|
| **should** / **shouldn't** | conseil, recommandation | conseil simple | You should sleep eight hours a night. |
| **ought to** / **ought not to** | conseil, ce qui est juste | conseil simple, un peu plus formel | You ought to eat less salt. |
| **had better** ('d better) / **had better not** | conseil urgent, sinon problème | conseil fort | You'd better stop smoking, or you will get ill. |
| **must** / **mustn't** | obligation, interdiction | très fort (règle, ordre du médecin) | You must finish the treatment. You mustn't drink alcohol. |

### 3. La construction

**Affirmative :** sujet + modal + base verbale
- She **should eat** more greens. (et non : she should eats / she should to eat)

**Négative :** sujet + modal + not + base verbale
- You **shouldn't drink** so many sodas.
- You **had better not skip** your meals.

**Interrogative :** modal + sujet + base verbale ?
- **Should I see** a doctor?
- What **should we eat** before an exam?

### 4. Cinq exemples sur le thème

1. Children **should** drink milk every day.
2. People with diabetes **ought to** avoid sugar.
3. You **had better** wash your hands before eating.
4. Patients **must** follow the doctor's instructions.
5. We **shouldn't** eat fried food every day.

### 5. Erreurs fréquentes

| Faux | Correct | Pourquoi |
|---|---|---|
| You should to eat more fruit. | You should eat more fruit. | pas de « to » après should |
| He shoulds drink water. | He should drink water. | jamais de « s » au modal |
| You must eating well. | You must eat well. | base verbale, pas de -ing |
| You ought eat less sugar. | You ought to eat less sugar. | ought est toujours suivi de to |
| You had better to rest. | You had better rest. | pas de « to » après had better |
| Do you should see a doctor? | Should you see a doctor? | pas de « do » avec un modal |

### 6. Must ou have to ?

- **must** : l'obligation vient de celui qui parle ou d'une règle forte (« Tu dois finir ce traitement », dit le médecin).
- **have to** : l'obligation vient de l'extérieur (« I have to take my tablets at 8 o'clock »).
- Attention au négatif : **mustn't** = c'est interdit ; **don't have to** = ce n'est pas nécessaire.
  - You mustn't eat before the blood test. (interdit)
  - You don't have to pay: the consultation is free. (pas nécessaire)

### À toi

Les exercices de grammaire corrigés t'attendent dans le bouton « Exercices » en bas de page (exercices 1 à 3).

lessons.title: Listening — At the health centre
lessons.content:
## Listening — À la consultation

**Situation :** Grâce, élève de Terminale, se sent fatiguée depuis plusieurs semaines. Elle consulte le docteur Mavoungou au centre de santé de son quartier.

### Avant d'écouter

1. Regarde les mots-clés : tired (fatiguée), dizzy (prise de vertiges), breakfast, sodas, blood test (analyse de sang), anaemia (anémie).
2. Devine : à ton avis, pourquoi Grâce est-elle fatiguée ?

### Comment travailler

L'enregistrement audio de ce dialogue sera bientôt disponible dans l'application. En attendant :

- **Première écoute :** demande à un camarade ou à un parent de te lire le dialogue à voix haute, sans le regarder. Essaie de répondre aux questions de compréhension globale (exercice 4).
- **Deuxième écoute :** relis toi-même le texte ci-dessous et vérifie tes réponses, puis fais les questions de détail.
- **Troisième écoute :** lis-le à voix haute à deux, en jouant les rôles.

### Transcript — Transcription

**Doctor:** Good morning, Grâce. Please sit down. What's the problem?

**Grâce:** Good morning, doctor. I've been very tired for three weeks. I can't concentrate in class, and sometimes I feel dizzy when I stand up.

**Doctor:** I see. Do you sleep well?

**Grâce:** Not really. I study late, usually until one o'clock in the morning, because the baccalaureate is in June.

**Doctor:** And what do you eat during the day?

**Grâce:** Well, I usually skip breakfast because I'm in a hurry. At school I buy fritters and a soda. In the evening I eat cassava with a little fish.

**Doctor:** How many sodas do you drink a day?

**Grâce:** Two or three, I think.

**Doctor:** That's too much sugar, and not enough real food. Your tiredness may come from anaemia — a lack of iron in the blood. We are going to do a blood test to check.

**Grâce:** Is it serious?

**Doctor:** Not if you change your habits. First, you shouldn't skip breakfast: even some bread and an egg will help. You ought to eat more greens, like cassava leaves or spinach, and beans — they are rich in iron. And you'd better replace the sodas with water.

**Grâce:** What about my revision?

**Doctor:** Your brain needs rest too. You should go to bed before eleven. If the test shows anaemia, you must take the iron tablets every day for two months. Don't stop the treatment, even if you feel better.

**Grâce:** All right. Thank you, doctor.

**Doctor:** You're welcome. Come back next Friday with the results. And good luck with the bac!

### Vocabulaire clé du dialogue

| English | Français |
|---|---|
| I've been tired for three weeks | je suis fatiguée depuis trois semaines |
| to feel dizzy | avoir des vertiges |
| to be in a hurry | être pressé |
| fritters | des beignets |
| a lack of iron | un manque de fer |
| a blood test | une analyse de sang |
| tablets | des comprimés |
| the results | les résultats |

**Remarque de grammaire :** « I've been very tired for three weeks » utilise le present perfect avec for pour une situation qui dure encore. Tu le retrouveras dans une prochaine unité.

### Questions

Les questions de compréhension (globale puis détaillée) et leur corrigé sont dans l'**exercice 4**, en bas de page.

lessons.title: Reading — Eating well in a changing Africa
lessons.content:
## Reading — Comprendre un texte

### Avant de lire — Skimming

Lis seulement le titre et la première phrase de chaque paragraphe. Puis réponds : de quoi parle le texte en général ? (Une phrase suffit.)

### Eating well in a changing Africa

**1.** For centuries, African families ate what they grew: cassava, plantains, millet, beans, fish from the rivers and leaves from the garden. These foods were simple, but they were fresh and rich in fibre and vitamins. Today, especially in big cities like Brazzaville, Pointe-Noire or Kinshasa, eating habits are changing fast.

**2.** In the streets, young people can find cheap fritters, fried chicken, white bread and sweet sodas at every corner. Supermarkets sell imported products full of sugar, salt and fat. These foods are quick and tasty, and many students eat them every day because they have little time and little money. As a result, doctors observe a worrying rise in obesity, diabetes and high blood pressure, diseases that were once rare in Africa.

**3.** At the same time, malnutrition has not disappeared. In some rural areas and poor neighbourhoods, children still do not get enough proteins and vitamins to grow normally. Africa therefore faces a "double burden": too much bad food for some, not enough good food for others.

**4.** Yet the solution is often on our own plates. Traditional dishes such as saka-saka (cassava leaves), beans, fish and fresh fruit are healthy and usually cheaper than junk food. Health experts say that we should eat more vegetables and fruit, drink water instead of sodas, and reduce salt and sugar. They also remind us that we ought to stay active: walking to school or playing football is free exercise.

**5.** Governments and schools have a role to play too. Some countries now teach nutrition at school and tax sugary drinks. But the most important change starts with each of us. As the saying goes, "You are what you eat."

(Texte rédigé pour ce cours, environ 330 mots.)

### Mots utiles du texte

| English | Français |
|---|---|
| to grow (grew, grown) | cultiver, faire pousser ; grandir |
| fibre | les fibres |
| at every corner | à chaque coin de rue |
| a worrying rise | une hausse inquiétante |
| once rare | autrefois rare |
| a neighbourhood | un quartier |
| a burden | un fardeau |
| yet | pourtant |
| to tax | taxer |

### Stratégie de lecture

1. **Skimming** (lecture globale) : titre + premières phrases → idée générale.
2. **Scanning** (lecture ciblée) : chercher une information précise (un nom, un chiffre, un exemple).
3. **Deviner un mot inconnu** grâce au contexte avant d'ouvrir le dictionnaire : dans « a worrying rise in obesity », rise est suivi d'une maladie qui augmente… donc rise = hausse.

### Questions

Les questions (compréhension globale, détaillée, vocabulaire en contexte et interprétation) sont dans les **exercices 5 et 6**, en bas de page.

lessons.title: Speaking — Talking about your eating habits
lessons.content:
## Speaking — S'exprimer à l'oral

### 1. Discussion questions — Questions de discussion

Réponds à voix haute, en faisant des phrases complètes. Utilise au moins un modal par réponse.

1. What do you usually eat for breakfast, lunch and dinner?
2. Do you think young people in Congo eat better or worse than their grandparents? Why?
3. What advice would you give to a friend who drinks too many sodas?
4. Should street food be sold near schools? Give two reasons.
5. What do you do to stay fit?

### 2. Phrases modèles — Model sentences

Répète ces phrases jusqu'à les dire sans lire :

| Pour… | Phrases |
|---|---|
| Parler de ses habitudes | I usually have… for breakfast. / I never skip lunch. / I eat fish twice a week. |
| Donner un conseil | You should… / You ought to… / If I were you, I would… / You'd better… |
| Donner son avis | In my opinion,… / I think that… / I strongly believe that… |
| Être d'accord ou non | I agree with you because… / I'm not sure about that. / I disagree, because… |
| Nuancer | It depends on… / On the one hand,… on the other hand,… |

### 3. Role-play — Jeu de rôle

Travaillez à deux. Inversez ensuite les rôles.

**Student A — the patient.** You often feel tired, you have headaches and you have gained weight. You eat fried food every day and you never exercise. Explain your problem and ask for advice.

**Student B — the doctor.** Ask questions about the patient's habits (sleep, food, drinks, sport). Then give at least **four pieces of advice** using should, ought to, had better and must.

Pour commencer :
- **Doctor:** Good afternoon. What can I do for you?
- **Patient:** Good afternoon, doctor. I've been feeling tired and…

### 4. Mini-débat

**Motion :** « Sugary drinks should be banned in schools. »

Formez deux groupes (for / against). Chaque groupe prépare trois arguments avec un exemple, puis répond aux arguments de l'autre groupe. Utilisez les connecteurs first, moreover, however, finally.

### Conseils pour l'oral

- Parle lentement et articule les fins de mots (diet, healthy, vitamins).
- Accentue la bonne syllabe : ˈhealthy, preˈvent, ˈvegetables (3 syllabes : /ˈvedʒtəblz/).
- Mieux vaut une phrase simple et juste qu'une phrase longue et fausse.

lessons.title: BAC — Thematic vocabulary (≈ 300 words)
lessons.content:
## Lexique thématique — Les mots du BAC, thème par thème

Apprends les mots par thème et fais des phrases avec eux. Pour chaque thème, le vocabulaire complet (prononciation, exemples) est dans la leçon Vocabulary de l'unité correspondante.

### 1. Food and health — Alimentation et santé

diet (régime alimentaire), balanced (équilibré), nutrition, nutrient (nutriment), vitamin, protein (protéine), calorie, meal (repas), to cook (cuisiner), to swallow (avaler), appetite, hunger (faim), thirst (soif), to starve (mourir de faim), malnutrition, obesity (obésité), overweight (en surpoids), junk food (malbouffe), to avoid (éviter), fresh (frais), rotten (pourri), disease / illness (maladie), to recover (guérir), cure (remède), treatment (traitement), to prevent (prévenir), hygiene, vaccine (vaccin), symptom, fit (en forme), to exercise (faire du sport), well-being (bien-être).

### 2. Development — Le développement

development, growth (croissance), economy, industry, agriculture, infrastructure, investment, resources, wealth (richesse), poverty (pauvreté), standard of living (niveau de vie), literacy (alphabétisation), education, progress, to improve (améliorer), sustainable (durable), aid (aide), debt (dette), loan (prêt), trade (commerce), export, import, developing country, developed country, inequality, welfare (protection sociale), to finance, policy (mesure politique), budget, rural, urban, to urbanise.

### 3. Music and sports — Musique et sport

music, song (chanson), singer (chanteur), musician, band (groupe), instrument, rhythm (rythme), melody, lyrics (paroles), concert, stage (scène), to perform (se produire), audience (public), team (équipe), player (joueur), coach (entraîneur), to train (s'entraîner), match, championship (championnat), tournament (tournoi), referee (arbitre), to compete (concourir), to win / to lose, to beat (battre), victory, defeat (défaite), fan / supporter, stadium, fitness (forme physique), talent, discipline, to cheer (encourager).

### 4. The North/South divide — La fracture Nord-Sud

the North / the South, divide (fracture), gap (écart), inequality, rich / poor, trade, raw materials (matières premières), finished goods (produits finis), exploitation, fair trade (commerce équitable), globalisation (mondialisation), debt, aid, cooperation, dependence, independence, colonialism, market, price, to export / to import, multinational, migration, refugee (réfugié), brain drain (fuite des cerveaux), solidarity, justice, to benefit from (profiter de), to exploit, added value (valeur ajoutée), emerging (émergent).

### 5. Famous lives — Vies célèbres

to be born (naître), childhood (enfance), to grow up (grandir), youth (jeunesse), career (carrière), achievement (réalisation), success (réussite), to struggle (lutter), to overcome (surmonter), hardship (épreuve), to dedicate one's life to (consacrer sa vie à), to fight for (se battre pour), freedom, leader (dirigeant), hero / heroine, role model (modèle), influence, legacy (héritage), fame (célébrité), famous, to inspire, award / prize (récompense, prix), to discover, invention, courage, sacrifice, reputation, to admire, biography.

### 6. Transport — Le transport

public transport (transports en commun), vehicle, car, bus, coach (autocar), train, railway (chemin de fer), plane, boat, canoe (pirogue), bicycle, motorbike taxi, road, traffic (circulation), traffic jam (embouteillage), rush hour (heure de pointe), fare (prix du billet), ticket, journey (trajet), trip (voyage court), to travel, to commute (faire la navette), passenger, driver, fuel (carburant), pollution, accident, safety (sécurité), speed (vitesse), delay (retard), crowded (bondé), reliable (fiable), affordable (abordable).

### 7. Demographic, ecological and social problems — Problèmes démographiques, écologiques et sociaux

population growth (croissance démographique), overpopulation, birth rate / death rate (taux de natalité / mortalité), rural exodus (exode rural), slum (bidonville), environment, climate change, global warming (réchauffement climatique), pollution, deforestation, waste / rubbish (déchets), to recycle, to pollute, to protect, to preserve, awareness (prise de conscience), unemployment (chômage), crime (criminalité), shortage (pénurie), drought (sécheresse), flood (inondation), famine, epidemic, soil erosion (érosion des sols), endangered species (espèces menacées), charcoal (charbon de bois), sustainable, to threaten (menacer), cause, consequence, solution.

### 8. Employment — L'emploi

job, work, employment, unemployment, employer / employee, to apply for (postuler), application (candidature), CV, cover letter (lettre de motivation), interview (entretien), skill (compétence), qualification, experience, training (formation), internship (stage), to hire (embaucher), to fire (licencier), to recruit, salary / wage (salaire), income (revenu), career, promotion, self-employed (indépendant), entrepreneur, business, to earn a living (gagner sa vie), workplace (lieu de travail), colleague, workforce (main-d'œuvre), part-time / full-time, vacancy (poste vacant).

### 9. Politics — La politique

government, the State (l'État), democracy, dictatorship (dictature), election, to elect (élire), to vote, ballot (bulletin), candidate, political party, citizen (citoyen), citizenship, rights / duties (droits / devoirs), freedom of speech (liberté d'expression), law (loi), justice, to govern, power, leader, president, parliament, minister, policy, corruption, bribery (pots-de-vin), accountable (qui rend des comptes), peace, war, conflict, human rights, constitution, majority, opposition, the common good (l'intérêt général).

### Comment réviser ce lexique

- Un thème par jour : lis la liste, cache le français, puis cache l'anglais.
- Écris **trois phrases** par thème avec cinq mots de la liste.
- Avant un sujet type BAC, relis la liste du thème du texte : tu comprendras plus vite.
