exercises.title: Devoir Chaminade 2021-2022 (Tle C-D) — Eating too much salt
exercises.statement:
**Lycée Chaminade, département de LVE, section anglais — 2021-2022 — Premier devoir du deuxième trimestre — Terminale C et D — Anglais — 3 heures**

## SECTION ONE: Reading
Read carefully the text below and then answer the related questions.

**TEXT: Eating too much salt**
> *Text adapted for the app from an article by Rebecca Howard (2018): same ideas, different wording.*

Salt is added to food to make it tastier. It provides the body with sodium, which is necessary for the muscles to work properly and for regulating the amount of water in the body. Health experts advise most adults to keep their daily sodium intake around 1,500 milligrams and never above 2,300 milligrams: eating more than this maximum is harmful.

High blood pressure, also called hypertension, affects millions of people. It can be caused by other factors, such as stress or a diet rich in saturated fats, but eating too much sodium increases the risk of developing it. For people who already suffer from high blood pressure, eating less salt can also reduce the risk of heart disease and stroke.

Fluid retention, also known as oedema, happens when too much water builds up in the body, including under the skin. It can be caused by hormone changes, hot weather and a high salt intake. It shows as swelling in the hands, ankles and feet, with a feeling of stiffness or pain. Eating less salt and drinking plenty of water can help to alleviate this condition.

Scientists have not yet proved a definite link between salt and heart disease, but most studies agree that too much salt increases the risk. Sodium causes the body to keep water, which raises blood pressure; high blood pressure, in turn, increases the risk of heart attack and stroke. That is why many doctors prefer not to take any chances and advise everyone to reduce the salt in their food.

**A. Write true or false after the following statements (2 pts)**
1. Consuming too much salt through food could be harmful.
2. It is necessary to keep a check on how much salt you consume.
3. Consuming too much salt can leave you feeling thirsty most of the time.
4. A healthy diet is essential for both children and adults.

**B. Answer the following questions (4 pts)**
1. Why does everyone need salt?
2. What should be done to reduce the risk of diseases?
3. Is there any relationship between the food we eat and health? Justify.
4. Quote from the text the other factors of the diseases linked to too much salt intake.

## SECTION TWO: Linguistic competence
**A. Vocabulary (2 pts)** — Match the following words with their suitable synonym:
1. Intake — 2. Swelling — 3. Alleviate — 4. Stiffness
a. Hardness — b. Absorption — c. Puffiness — d. Diminish

**B. Grammar (4 pts)**
1. Complete these sentences with *much, many, a few, little*. (2 pts)
 1) How ……… juice is left in the bottle?
 2) I have had ……… headaches already because of the stress.
 3) We have ……… bread; it is not enough for dinner.
 4) Janie and Bob have ……… chairs but they need more.
2. Correct the mistake contained in each of the sentences below. (2 pts)
 1) She recommended me that I take a few days off from my work.
 2) I have not ate anything today.
 3) I hate doing mistakes.
 4) Please, borrow me your car.

## SECTION THREE: Communicative competence (4 pts)
Complete the following conversation with the missing parts.
A: Morning. — B: Morning. — A: ……1…… — B: Jane took the blue shirt to the cleaner. — A: ……2…… — B: After the trip John and Jake felt sick. — A: ……3…… — B: No, they didn't go to work by their own car. — A: ……4…… — B: Yes, they already left for work. — A: Bye.

## SECTION FOUR: Guided writing (4 pts)
Write in order these scrambled sentences.
1) Not / physician / most / diarrhoea / a / people / suffering / from / consult / do.
2) Healthy / ? / food / eat / do / you / brain / your / keep / to / any.
3) Near / a / parking / place / the / shops / rarely / they / find.
4) Parents / my / I / sometimes / fly / winter / to / in / Florida / to.

exercises.title: Exercise 2 — Used to
exercises.statement:
Réécris chaque phrase avec **used to** ou **didn't use to**.

1. When I was a child, I played football in the street every evening.
2. My grandfather sang in a rumba orchestra in his youth. (He doesn't any more.)
3. In the past, people didn't watch matches on their phones.
4. My sister danced ndombolo at every family party when she was young.
5. Before his injury, he trained every morning.

Puis pose la question correspondant à la phrase 1, avec **Did… use to…?**

exercises.title: Ejercicio 6 — Leer: vocabulario e interpretación
exercises.statement:
**A. Busca en el texto la palabra que significa:**
1. el cincuenta por ciento (párrafo 1)
2. una prueba difícil (párrafo 1)
3. pagar para usar algo durante un tiempo (párrafo 3)
4. la parte de la calle reservada a las personas que caminan (párrafo 5)
5. una persona que va a pie (párrafo 5)

**B.** Dans le paragraphe 5, à qui s'adressent les verbes « desarrollen, construyan, planten » ? À quelle personne sont-ils ? Donne leur infinitif.

**C. Interpretación (4-5 frases en español).**
6. «Una ciudad más fácil de recorrer es también una ciudad más humana». ¿Qué significa? Propón dos soluciones para tu ciudad, con el imperativo.

exercises.title: Ejercicio 2 — Tú o usted
exercises.statement:
**A. Transforme ces instructions données à un ami (tú) en instructions polies à une dame âgée (usted).**
1. Sigue todo recto.
2. Gira a la izquierda.
3. Toma la segunda calle.
4. Cruza el puente.
5. Coge el taxi.
6. Sube al autobús.

**B. Fais l'inverse : transforme en forme tú.**
7. Baje en la tercera parada.
8. Vuelva mañana.
9. Vaya al hospital.
10. Venga conmigo.

exercises.title: Ejercicio 5 — Leer: comprensión del texto
exercises.statement:
Réponds aux questions sur le texte « Moverse en la ciudad: un desafío diario ».

**A. Comprensión global**
1. El texto: (a) es una guía turística de Madrid (b) presenta los problemas de transporte de tres ciudades y propone soluciones (c) cuenta un viaje en avión.

**B. Comprensión detallada**
2. ¿Qué parte de la población del mundo vive en ciudades?
3. Cita tres problemas de la vida urbana.
4. ¿Cómo se desplaza la mayoría de la gente en Brazzaville?
5. ¿Por qué muchos estudiantes caminan varios kilómetros cada día?
6. Cita tres medios de transporte de Madrid.
7. ¿Qué ha decidido el ayuntamiento de Madrid? ¿Por qué?
8. ¿Por qué el avión y el barco son importantes en Malabo?
9. Cita dos consejos para las ciudades y dos consejos para los ciudadanos.

**C. ¿Verdadero o falso? Justifica con una frase del texto.**
10. En Madrid, nadie usa el coche.

exercises.title: Ejercicio 3 — Pronombres y corrección de errores
exercises.statement:
**A. Ajoute le pronom à l'impératif (n'oublie pas l'accent écrit).**
1. llamar + me (tú) → ______
2. decir + me (tú) → ______
3. esperar + nos (tú) → ______
4. decir + me (usted) → ______

**B. Chaque phrase contient une erreur. Corrige-la.**
5. Señor, ¡gira a la izquierda, por favor!
6. Sigua todo recto.
7. ¡Sale de casa ahora!
8. Cruze la calle aquí.
9. Me llama cuando llegues. (sens : appelle-moi)
10. Voy al instituto en pie.

exercises.title: Ejercicio 2 — Participios irregulares y pronombres
exercises.statement:
**A. Mets au pretérito perfecto (attention aux participes irréguliers).**
1. El médico me ______ (escribir) una receta.
2. ¿Qué te ______ (decir) la enfermera?
3. Esta mañana yo ______ (hacer) deporte.
4. Mi primo ______ (romperse) la pierna jugando al fútbol.
5. La farmacia ______ (abrir) a las ocho.
6. ¿Tú ______ (ver) al médico hoy?
7. La enfermera me ______ (poner) una inyección.
8. Mi padre ya ______ (volver) del hospital.

**B. Complète avec me duele ou me duelen.**
9. ______ la garganta.
10. ______ los ojos.

exercises.title: Ejercicio 3 — Ya, todavía no, nunca y corrección de errores
exercises.statement:
**A. Réponds avec ya ou todavía no + pretérito perfecto, et un pronom quand c'est possible.**
1. ¿Ya has tomado el jarabe? — Sí, ______.
2. ¿Ya has hecho el test? — No, ______.
3. ¿Has tenido paludismo alguna vez? — No, ______ (nunca).

**B. Chaque phrase contient une erreur. Corrige-la.**
4. Soy ido a la farmacia.
5. Me soy caído en el patio.
6. He hacido un análisis de sangre.
7. He ya tomado las pastillas.
8. La doctora ha escrita la receta.
9. Me duele mi cabeza.
10. Mi hermana está embarazada porque ha olvidado los deberes. (sens voulu : elle est gênée)

exercises.title: Ejercicio 6 — Leer: vocabulario e interpretación
exercises.statement:
**A. Busca en el texto la palabra o expresión que significa:**
1. muy viejo (párrafo 1)
2. el agua que no se mueve (párrafo 2)
3. una mujer que espera un bebé (párrafo 2)
4. que funciona bien, que da resultado (párrafo 4)
5. un trabajo, una misión (párrafo 5)

**B.** Pourquoi l'auteur utilise-t-il le pretérito perfecto dans « se han distribuido millones de mosquiteras » ? Donne l'infinitif de « distribuido » et de « han empezado ».

**C. Interpretación (4-5 frases en español).**
6. «La lucha contra el paludismo es una tarea de todos». Explica esta frase y di qué has hecho tú o qué hace tu familia para prevenir el paludismo.

exercises.title: Ejercicio 9 — Escribir: mi salud y mis buenos propósitos (120-150 palabras)
exercises.statement:
**Tema :** Ton correspondant t'écrit qu'il a été malade. Réponds-lui (**120 à 150 mots**) : prends de ses nouvelles, raconte ce qui t'est arrivé récemment, explique ce que tu as fait cette semaine pour rester en bonne santé et donne-lui deux conseils.

Suis le plan de la leçon Escribir. Utilise au moins six pretéritos perfectos, dont deux participes irréguliers. Écris ton texte, valide-le, puis compare avec l'exemple corrigé.

exercises.title: Exercise 1 — Will: predictions and decisions
exercises.statement:
**A. Complète avec will ou won't + le verbe entre parenthèses.**
1. I think the new road ______ (reduce) traffic jams.
2. Don't worry, the bus ______ (be) late today, the driver is always on time.
3. In 2050, most cars ______ (run) on electricity.
4. ______ the train ______ (stop) at Dolisie?
5. She doesn't like planes. She ______ (fly) to Pointe-Noire.

**B. Réagis à chaque situation avec une décision prise sur le moment (I'll…).**
6. Your grandmother has a heavy bag.
7. You missed the last bus.
8. Your friend doesn't know the way to the station.

exercises.title: End-of-unit test — Writing and speaking tasks
exercises.statement:
Ces deux tâches complètent le **QCM de fin d'unité** (20 questions).

**1. Writing task (70-90 words).** Write an email to a friend about a trip you are going to make during the next holidays: where you are going to go, how you are going to travel, and what you think the journey will be like.

**2. Speaking task.** Enregistre-toi pendant **1 minute 30** : « How will people travel in Congo in 2050? »

exercises.title: Ejercicio 1 — Conjuga en futuro (verbos regulares)
exercises.statement:
Mets les verbes au **futur simple**.

1. El año que viene, yo ______ (estudiar) Derecho.
2. ¿Tú ______ (trabajar) en una empresa o por cuenta propia?
3. Mi hermana ______ (ser) enfermera.
4. Nosotros ______ (vivir) en Pointe-Noire.
5. ¿Vosotros ______ (buscar) trabajo en verano?
6. Mis primos ______ (abrir) una tienda en el mercado.
7. En el futuro, los agricultores ______ (usar) nuevas técnicas.
8. Yo te ______ (escribir) cuando tenga noticias.

exercises.title: Ejercicio 4 — Escuchar: ¿Qué harás después del bachillerato?
exercises.statement:
Réponds aux questions sur l'entretien d'orientation (leçon Escuchar). Réponds en espagnol, par des phrases complètes.

**A. Comprensión global — ¿Verdadero o falso?**
1. Arnaud y Prisca tienen un proyecto muy claro.
2. La consejera aconseja a Arnaud la formación profesional.
3. Prisca quiere trabajar en un banco.

**B. Comprensión detallada**
4. ¿Qué quieren los padres de Arnaud?
5. ¿Qué le gusta hacer a Arnaud?
6. Según la consejera, ¿por qué Arnaud nunca estará en paro?
7. ¿Qué podrá hacer Arnaud dentro de unos años?
8. ¿Qué estudiará Prisca? ¿Por qué?
9. ¿Cuáles son las etapas del proyecto de Prisca? (tres)
10. ¿Qué hará la empresa de Prisca?
11. Según la consejera, ¿cuál será uno de los sectores más importantes del futuro?

exercises.title: Exercise 5 — Reading: understanding the text
exercises.statement:
Réponds aux questions sur le texte « African cities on the move ».

**A. Global understanding**
1. The text is mainly about: (a) the history of the African railway (b) the transport problems of African cities and some solutions (c) how to buy a car.

**B. Detailed understanding**
2. How much time can workers spend travelling every day?
3. What will happen to the population of African cities, according to experts?
4. What did Addis Ababa open in 2015?
5. Why are the buses of Dar es Salaam faster?
6. What change is happening in Kigali, Nairobi and Kampala? Give two advantages.
7. Explain the comparison with the mobile phone.
8. Give two difficulties of building modern transport.
9. What is the change in the Tanzanian commuter's life?

**C. True or False? Justify.**
10. The best projects exclude the informal transport workers.

exercises.title: Ejercicio 2 — Futuro irregular
exercises.statement:
Mets les verbes au **futur simple** (attention aux radicaux irréguliers).

1. Yo ______ (tener) mi propio taller.
2. ¿______ (poder) tú ayudar a tu familia?
3. Mi primo ______ (hacer) prácticas en un banco.
4. En 2050, ______ (haber) más empleos en la informática.
5. Nosotros ______ (salir) del instituto en junio.
6. La consejera nos ______ (decir) qué formación elegir.
7. Mis padres ______ (venir) a la ceremonia.
8. Algún día tú ______ (saber) hablar cinco idiomas.
9. ¿Dónde ______ (poner) usted su empresa?
10. ¿______ (querer) vosotros trabajar conmigo?

exercises.title: Ejercicio 5 — Leer: comprensión del texto
exercises.statement:
Réponds aux questions sur le texte « Los trabajos del futuro ».

**A. Comprensión global**
1. El texto: (a) cuenta la vida de un empresario (b) presenta los sectores que crearán empleo en el futuro y las cualidades necesarias (c) explica cómo escribir un currículum.

**B. Comprensión detallada**
2. ¿Qué pregunta se hacen todos los jóvenes que terminan sus estudios?
3. ¿Dónde trabaja una gran parte de la población en muchos países africanos? Da dos ejemplos.
4. ¿Qué trabajos aumentarán gracias a la tecnología?
5. ¿Por qué la agricultura será un sector clave? (dos razones)
6. ¿Cómo trabajarán los agricultores del futuro?
7. ¿Qué son los «empleos verdes»? Da dos ejemplos.
8. ¿Por qué los oficios manuales seguirán siendo necesarios?
9. ¿Qué cualidades buscarán los empleadores? (tres)

**C. ¿Verdadero o falso? Justifica con una frase del texto.**
10. En el futuro, un diploma será suficiente para encontrar trabajo.

exercises.title: Exercise 6 — Reading: vocabulary and interpretation
exercises.statement:
**A. Find in the text a word or expression that means:**
1. full of people or vehicles (paragraph 1)
2. to become two times bigger (paragraph 1)
3. a part of a road reserved for some vehicles (paragraph 2)
4. to jump over a stage (paragraph 3)
5. not too expensive (paragraph 5)

**B.** Paragraph 1: "If nothing changes, traffic will become even worse." Identify the grammar structure and explain its use.

**C. Interpretation (4-5 sentences).**
6. "Clean, safe and affordable transport is not a luxury." Do you agree? Explain with examples from your town.

exercises.title: Exercise 5 — Reading: understanding the text
exercises.statement:
Réponds aux questions sur le texte « The Congo Basin, the green lungs of Africa ».

**A. Global understanding**
1. The text mainly explains: (a) how to visit the Congo Basin as a tourist (b) the importance of the Congo Basin forest, the threats against it and some solutions (c) the history of the Republic of the Congo.

**B. Detailed understanding**
2. Which is the largest tropical rainforest in the world? And the second?
3. How many countries share the Congo Basin forest? Name three.
4. Why is it called "the green lungs of Africa"?
5. What was discovered in 2017, and where?
6. What will happen if the peatland is drained or burnt?
7. Give four human activities that threaten the forest.
8. Why does population growth increase the pressure on the forest?
9. Give three solutions mentioned in paragraph 4.

**C. True or False? Justify.**
10. The forest can be protected without the local communities.

exercises.title: Exercise 9 — Writing: an essay on a local problem (150-180 words)
exercises.statement:
**Topic:** Choose one problem of your town or country (plastic waste, deforestation, rural exodus, youth unemployment, erosion…). Explain its causes and consequences, and suggest solutions (**150 to 180 words**).

Suis le plan de la leçon Writing. Utilise au moins trois connecteurs de cause ou de conséquence et trois phrases passives. Écris ton texte, valide-le, puis compare avec l'exemple corrigé.

exercises.title: Ejercicio 1 — Conjuga en pretérito indefinido (verbos regulares)
exercises.statement:
Mets les verbes au **pretérito indefinido**.

1. Ayer yo ______ (bailar) toda la noche.
2. ¿Tú ______ (ver) el partido? (attention : ver est irrégulier)
3. El cantante ______ (cantar) tres canciones nuevas.
4. Nosotros ______ (comer) en casa de mi tía.
5. ¿Vosotros ______ (salir) el sábado?
6. Mis amigos ______ (llegar) tarde al concierto.
7. Mi hermana ______ (escribir) una canción.
8. El sábado pasado yo ______ (jugar) al baloncesto.

exercises.title: Ejercicio 4 — Escuchar: ¿Qué hiciste el fin de semana?
exercises.statement:
Réponds aux questions sur le dialogue (leçon Escuchar). Réponds en espagnol, par des phrases complètes.

**A. Comprensión global — ¿Verdadero o falso?**
1. Santiago y Divine pasaron el fin de semana juntos.
2. El equipo de Santiago ganó el partido.
3. Divine descansó el domingo.

**B. Comprensión detallada**
4. ¿Contra quién jugó el equipo de Santiago?
5. ¿Cuántos goles marcó Santiago? ¿Cuál fue el resultado final?
6. ¿Qué hicieron sus compañeros y el entrenador después del partido?
7. ¿Qué hizo Santiago el domingo? (tres actividades)
8. ¿Adónde fue Divine el sábado por la noche? ¿Con quién?
9. ¿Por qué tuvieron que esperar dos horas?
10. ¿Qué hizo la prima Grâce?
11. ¿A qué hora volvió Divine a casa? ¿Qué hizo el domingo?

exercises.title: Ejercicio 7 — Vocabulario: relaciona y completa
exercises.statement:
**A. Relie chaque mot à sa définition.**

| Palabra | Definición |
|---|---|
| 1. el árbitro | a. el lugar donde cantan los artistas en un concierto |
| 2. el escenario | b. la persona que hace respetar las reglas del partido |
| 3. empatar | c. las palabras de una canción |
| 4. la letra | d. terminar un partido con el mismo resultado |
| 5. el entrenador | e. la persona que prepara a los jugadores |

**B. Completa con: toca, juega, concierto, gol, me encantan.**
6. Mi primo ______ la guitarra en una orquesta.
7. Mi hermana ______ al baloncesto.
8. ______ las canciones de rumba.
9. El delantero marcó un ______ en el último minuto.
10. Anoche fui a un ______ en el centro.

exercises.title: Exercise 1 — The passive: present and past
exercises.statement:
**A. Mets les phrases au passif (présent simple). N'ajoute pas l'agent s'il est inutile.**
1. People throw plastic bags into the gutters.
2. They collect the rubbish every Monday.
3. Factories pollute the river.
4. People use charcoal for cooking.

**B. Mets les phrases au passif (prétérit).**
5. The flood destroyed fifty houses.
6. Volunteers cleaned the beach.
7. Somebody stole my bicycle.
8. The government created a national park in 1935.

exercises.title: Exercise 7 — Vocabulary: match and complete
exercises.statement:
**A. Relie chaque mot à sa définition.**

| Word | Definition |
|---|---|
| 1. rural exodus | a. a poor area of a city with bad housing |
| 2. a slum | b. a long period without rain |
| 3. drought | c. the movement of people from the countryside to the cities |
| 4. endangered species | d. the situation of people who have no job |
| 5. unemployment | e. animals or plants that may disappear |

**B. Complète avec : recycled, awareness, deforestation, charcoal, flood.**
6. Most urban families cook with ______.
7. The ______ destroyed many houses near the river.
8. Plastic bottles can be ______ into paving stones.
9. The club wants to raise ______ about plastic waste.
10. ______ is the cutting down of forests on a large scale.

exercises.title: End-of-unit test — Writing and speaking tasks
exercises.statement:
Ces deux tâches complètent le **QCM de fin d'unité** (20 questions).

**1. Writing task (70-90 words).** Write a short news report about an environmental event in your town (a clean-up, a flood, a tree-planting day…). Use at least **four passive sentences**.

**2. Speaking task.** Enregistre-toi pendant **1 minute 30** : « Why do young people leave the villages? What are the consequences for the villages and the cities? »

exercises.title: Short reading texts 1 to 5 — quick training
exercises.statement:
**Entraînement rapide au Reading.** Lis chaque texte et réponds aux questions par des phrases complètes.

**Text 1 — Food and health**
> Many students skip breakfast, thinking they save time. In fact, they lose energy and concentration for the whole morning. The brain needs fuel to work, and breakfast is the best fuel of the day. A simple meal of bread, fruit and milk is enough. Students who eat a good breakfast remember their lessons better and feel less tired. So the few minutes "saved" by skipping breakfast are, in truth, minutes lost.

1. Why do students skip breakfast? 2. What does the brain need to work? 3. Give an example of a simple breakfast. 4. What advantage do students who eat breakfast have? 5. Why are the minutes "saved" really "lost"?

**Text 2 — Development**
> A road is more than stones and tar. When a new road reaches a village, children can go to school more easily, farmers can sell their crops in town, and sick people can reach a hospital. In this way, a single road can change many lives at once. This is why development experts say that infrastructure is the backbone of progress: without roads, water and electricity, even the best ideas stay on paper.

1. A road is "more than" what? 2. Name three changes a new road brings to a village. 3. What do experts call infrastructure? 4. What three examples of infrastructure are given? 5. What happens to ideas without infrastructure?

**Text 3 — Music and sports**
> When the national team plays, something strange happens: people who never speak to each other suddenly become friends. In the street, in the market, everyone talks about the same match. For ninety minutes, differences of tribe, religion and wealth seem to disappear. This is the hidden power of sport: it unites a nation around a shared emotion. Music does the same thing. A popular song can bring a whole country to its feet.

1. What "strange" thing happens during a national match? 2. Where do people talk about the match? 3. What differences "seem to disappear"? 4. What is "the hidden power of sport"? 5. What can music do, according to the text?

**Text 4 — The North/South divide**
> A farmer in the South grows cocoa and sells it very cheaply. Thousands of kilometres away, in the North, a factory turns that same cocoa into expensive chocolate. The farmer earns a few coins; the factory earns a fortune. This simple story explains much of the North/South divide. The solution is not charity but justice: if Southern countries could process their own raw materials, they would keep the profit at home.

1. What does the Southern farmer grow, and how does he sell it? 2. What does the Northern factory do with the cocoa? 3. Compare what each one earns. 4. What does this story explain? 5. What solution does the text propose?

**Text 5 — Famous lives**
> Wangari Maathai was a woman from Kenya who understood a simple truth: to protect people, you must protect nature. She founded a movement that planted millions of trees. At first people laughed, then they followed her. In 2004 she received the Nobel Peace Prize — the first African woman to do so. Her life proves that one determined person, armed only with an idea and courage, can change a nation.

1. Where was Wangari Maathai from? 2. What "simple truth" did she understand? 3. What did her movement do? 4. What prize did she receive, and when? 5. What does her life prove?

exercises.title: Short reading texts 6 to 10 — quick training
exercises.statement:
**Entraînement rapide au Reading.** Lis chaque texte et réponds aux questions par des phrases complètes.

**Text 6 — Transport**
> In our growing cities, the same scene repeats every morning: long lines of cars, horns, and clouds of smoke. People spend hours in traffic instead of being at work or at school. The problem is not that there are too many people, but too few good buses and trains. A single bus can carry fifty passengers; fifty cars carry the same fifty people, but fill the whole road. The answer to traffic is not wider roads, but better public transport.

1. What scene repeats every morning? 2. Where should people be, instead of in traffic? 3. According to the text, what is the real problem? 4. Compare a bus and fifty cars. 5. What is "the answer to traffic"?

**Text 7 — Demographic, ecological and social problems**
> Every year, our cities grow by thousands of new arrivals. They come from the countryside, hoping for a better life. But when a city grows faster than its houses, schools and jobs, slums appear at its edges. There, families live without clean water or electricity. The solution is not to close the cities, but to develop the countryside too, so that people are not forced to leave their villages. Balanced development is the best answer to uncontrolled urban growth.

1. Who are the "new arrivals", and where do they come from? 2. Why do they come to the city? 3. When do slums appear? 4. What do families in slums live without? 5. What solution does the text propose?

**Text 8 — Employment**
> Awa finished school with good results but could not find a job for two years. Instead of waiting, she used her small savings to buy a sewing machine. She began making clothes for her neighbours. Today she owns a small workshop and employs three young people. Awa's story shows that, in a country where jobs are rare, creating your own work is sometimes the wisest choice. Self-employment turns a job-seeker into a job-maker.

1. What was Awa's situation after school? 2. What did she buy with her savings? 3. What did she begin to do? 4. What does she own today, and whom does she employ? 5. Explain the last sentence.

**Text 9 — Politics**
> Some young people say: "Politics is not my business." But politics decides the price of bread, the quality of schools and the safety of streets. To ignore politics is to let others decide your life for you. Being a good citizen does not mean shouting the loudest; it means voting, respecting the law, paying taxes and refusing corruption. Democracy is not a gift that leaders give; it is a garden that citizens must water every day.

1. What do some young people say about politics? 2. Name three things politics decides. 3. What does it mean "to ignore politics"? 4. What does being a good citizen mean, according to the text? 5. Explain the image of the "garden".

**Text 10 — Health and development**
> Clean water is the simplest medicine in the world. Many diseases that fill our hospitals come from dirty water. Where families can drink safe water, children fall ill less often and go to school more regularly. This is why bringing clean water to a village is at the same time a question of health and of development. Sometimes the greatest progress does not come from complicated machines, but from a simple, clean well.

1. What is called "the simplest medicine in the world"? 2. Where do many diseases come from? 3. What happens where families drink safe water? 4. Why is clean water a question of both health and development? 5. What does the last sentence suggest about progress?

exercises.title: Ejercicio 3 — ¿Indefinido o perfecto? Corrige los errores
exercises.statement:
**A. Choisis entre l'indefinido et le perfecto selon le marqueur de temps.**

2. Esta semana ______ (yo, ir) dos veces a la playa.

4. ¿______ (tú, estar) alguna vez en un concierto?
5. Hace dos años mi equipo ______ (ganar) el campeonato.

**B. Chaque phrase contient une erreur. Corrige-la.**
6. Ayer jugo al fútbol con mis amigos.
7. Él bailo con mi prima.
8. Hací los deberes antes del partido.
9. Ayer he ido a un concierto.
10. Fué un partido increíble.

exercises.title: Ejercicio 6 — Leer: vocabulario e interpretación
exercises.statement:
**A. Busca en el texto la palabra o expresión que significa:**
1. un período de cien años (párrafo 2)
2. poner juntas cosas diferentes (párrafo 2)
3. crear una organización (párrafo 3)
4. el sentimiento de estar contento de algo propio (párrafo 4)
5. ser de alguien (párrafo 5)

**B.** Relève dans le paragraphe 3 quatre verbes à l'indefinido et donne leur infinitif. Pourquoi l'auteur utilise-t-il ce temps ?

exercises.title: Short reading texts 6 to 10 — quick training
exercises.statement:
**Entraînement rapide au Reading.** Lis chaque texte et réponds aux questions par des phrases complètes.

**Text 6 — Transport**
> In our growing cities, the same scene repeats every morning: long lines of cars, horns, and clouds of smoke. People spend hours in traffic instead of being at work or at school. The problem is not that there are too many people, but too few good buses and trains. A single bus can carry fifty passengers; fifty cars carry the same fifty people, but fill the whole road. The answer to traffic is not wider roads, but better public transport.

1. What scene repeats every morning? 2. Where should people be, instead of in traffic? 3. According to the text, what is the real problem? 4. Compare a bus and fifty cars. 5. What is "the answer to traffic"?

**Text 7 — Demographic, ecological and social problems**
> Every year, our cities grow by thousands of new arrivals. They come from the countryside, hoping for a better life. But when a city grows faster than its houses, schools and jobs, slums appear at its edges. There, families live without clean water or electricity. The solution is not to close the cities, but to develop the countryside too, so that people are not forced to leave their villages. Balanced development is the best answer to uncontrolled urban growth.

1. Who are the "new arrivals", and where do they come from? 2. Why do they come to the city? 3. When do slums appear? 4. What do families in slums live without? 5. What solution does the text propose?

**Text 8 — Employment**
> Awa finished school with good results but could not find a job for two years. Instead of waiting, she used her small savings to buy a sewing machine. She began making clothes for her neighbours. Today she owns a small workshop and employs three young people. Awa's story shows that, in a country where jobs are rare, creating your own work is sometimes the wisest choice. Self-employment turns a job-seeker into a job-maker.

1. What was Awa's situation after school? 2. What did she buy with her savings? 3. What did she begin to do? 4. What does she own today, and whom does she employ? 5. Explain the last sentence.

**Text 9 — Politics**
> Some young people say: "Politics is not my business." But politics decides the price of bread, the quality of schools and the safety of streets. To ignore politics is to let others decide your life for you. Being a good citizen does not mean shouting the loudest; it means voting, respecting the law, paying taxes and refusing corruption. Democracy is not a gift that leaders give; it is a garden that citizens must water every day.

1. What do some young people say about politics? 2. Name three things politics decides. 3. What does it mean "to ignore politics"? 4. What does being a good citizen mean, according to the text? 5. Explain the image of the "garden".

**Text 10 — Health and development**
> Clean water is the simplest medicine in the world. Many diseases that fill our hospitals come from dirty water. Where families can drink safe water, children fall ill less often and go to school more regularly. This is why bringing clean water to a village is at the same time a question of health and of development. Sometimes the greatest progress does not come from complicated machines, but from a simple, clean well.

1. What is called "the simplest medicine in the world"? 2. Where do many diseases come from? 3. What happens where families drink safe water? 4. Why is clean water a question of both health and development? 5. What does the last sentence suggest about progress?
